relations.summary: Confirmation bias compounds commitment bias by making the operator search for evidence that justifies the existing commitment.
Commitment-bias conflicts with confirmation-bias when the drive for consistency with past choices biases evidence evaluation toward confirming the original decision.
Confirmation-bias makes comparative-advantage defend an existing role map even after the evidence says the allocation is wrong.
Confirmation-bias distorts comparative-political-systems-analysis when analysts interpret cross-system evidence to defend a preferred political frame.
Comparative-political-systems-analysis conflicts with confirmation-bias when motivated reasoning distorts cross-system evidence toward a preferred framework.

Confirmation-bias turns compounding dangerous when people keep scaling a flawed thesis instead of checking whether the foundation is wrong.
Confirmation-bias corrupts confidence-calibration by defending a favored belief instead of updating confidence against disconfirming evidence.

Cognitive-dissonance powers confirmation bias by making inconsistent information psychologically painful — the discomfort of conflicting beliefs drives the bias to selectively filter incoming evidence so that new information aligns with previous decisions or self-image.
Confirmation-bias conflicts with critical-thinking when critical thinking insists on weighing all evidence instead of only confirming material.
Dialectical reasoning opposes confirmation bias by institutionalizing challenge and antithesis before synthesis.
Confirmation-bias conflicts with falsifiability when disproof standards challenge belief-preserving evidence selection.
The Feynman Technique counters confirmation bias by forcing blind spots and missing evidence into the open.
Intellectual-humility directly counters confirmation bias by replacing the ego-protective drive to confirm existing beliefs with the disposition to genuinely question whether one's view is optimal.
Rationalization helps confirmation-bias survive by laundering preferred conclusions into respectable stories after disconfirming evidence has already been filtered out.

System-1 is the cognitive engine that generates and sustains confirmation bias — automatic pattern-matching builds a coherent story from confirming evidence and suppresses ambiguity before deliberate reasoning can intervene.
Confirmation bias drives the fallacy by making the team collect only evidence that supports the optimistic sequential plan.

Correlation-vs-causation conflicts with confirmation-bias when observed correlations are selectively elevated to causal status because they confirm a pre-existing theory.
Confirmation-bias undermines counterfactual-reasoning by resisting the search for plausible opposite explanations.
Counterfactual-reasoning conflicts with confirmation-bias when teams search for support for the winning story instead of realistic alternatives.
